za-agter-paarl.name: Agter-Paarl
za-agter-paarl.grapes: Shiraz, Pinotage, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-agter-paarl.summary: The country 'behind' (agter) Paarl Mountain to the west, towards the Swartland, where Fairview's Charles Back farms goats and vines and makes Rhône-style wines and cheese. It is warmer and drier than the Paarl valley.
za-agter-paarl.terroir: Granite-derived soils and shale on gentle slopes; warm and dry.

za-agterkliphoogte.name: Agterkliphoogte
za-agterkliphoogte.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-agterkliphoogte.summary: A ward in the Agterkliphoogte valley near Robertson. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

za-ashton.name: Ashton
za-ashton.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-ashton.summary: A ward around the town of Ashton at the foot of the Langeberg. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

za-bamboes-bay.name: Bamboes Bay
za-bamboes-bay.summary: One of South Africa's smallest wards, on the Atlantic coast north of Lamberts Bay, where Fryer's Cove's vineyards lie a few hundred metres from the ocean. Its Sauvignon Blanc is lean and saline.
za-bamboes-bay.terroir: Sandy and limestone soils, cold Benguela fog.

za-banghoek.name: Banghoek
za-banghoek.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Chardonnay
za-banghoek.summary: A high mountain bowl at the top of the Helshoogte Pass between Stellenbosch and Franschhoek, surrounded by the Simonsberg, Jonkershoek and Groot Drakenstein ranges. Cooler and wetter than the valley below, it gives fresh, elegant Bordeaux varieties and Chardonnay.
za-banghoek.terroir: Granite and sandstone soils at about 400 to 600 m; high rainfall.

za-blouvlei.name: Blouvlei
za-blouvlei.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-blouvlei.summary: A ward of the Wellington district on the slopes and plain below the Hawequa mountains. It is one of five Wellington wards on the February 2026 Wine of Origin list; most producers still label their wine WO Wellington.

za-boesmansrivier.name: Boesmansrivier
za-boesmansrivier.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-boesmansrivier.summary: A ward along the Boesmans River near Bonnievale. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

za-bonnievale.name: Bonnievale
za-bonnievale.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-bonnievale.summary: A ward around Bonnievale on the Breede River, known for dairy and wine co-operatives. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate.

za-bot-river.name: Bot River
za-bot-river.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Pinotage, Shiraz, Sauvignon Blanc
za-bot-river.summary: The gateway to Walker Bay, from the Bot River lagoon into the foothills of the Groenlandberg and Babylonstoren ranges, bordering the Kogelberg Biosphere. Beaumont, in the village, has old Chenin and Pinotage; Gabrielskloof, Wildekrans and Barton are nearby. Afternoon winds blow up the valley off the sea.
za-bot-river.terroir: Mainly Bokkeveld shale (Glen Rosa and Klapmuts soils) and Table Mountain sandstone.

za-bottelary.name: Bottelary
za-bottelary.grapes: Pinotage, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-bottelary.summary: The Bottelary Hills north-west of Stellenbosch, a ridge of granite with views to Table Mountain, is old-vine Chenin and Pinotage country. Bellevue, in these hills, made the Pinotage that won the 1959 Cape Wine Show, and Kaapzicht, Hartenberg, Mooiplaas and Bellevue still farm old bush vines.
za-bottelary.terroir: Decomposed granite on the upper slopes and shale lower down; open to Atlantic breezes from the west.

za-bovlei.name: Bovlei
za-bovlei.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-bovlei.summary: A ward of Wellington in the upper Bovlei valley towards the Bainskloof Pass, home of the historic Bovlei co-operative cellar (1907). It is one of five Wellington wards on the February 2026 Wine of Origin list; most producers still label their wine WO Wellington.

za-breede-river-valley.name: Breede River Valley
za-breede-river-valley.summary: The inland region of the Breedekloof, Worcester and Robertson districts, warm and irrigated, the source of a large share of South Africa's wine and brandy. The region crushes a large share of South Africa's grapes, most of it through co-operative cellars.

za-breedekloof.name: Breedekloof
za-breedekloof.summary: A district around Rawsonville in the upper Breede River and its tributaries, below the Du Toitskloof mountains. Its large co-operatives once sent most fruit to distillers; now cellars such as Badsberg, Slanghoek and Goudini bottle good-value Chenin, and its old vineyards are sought by Stellenbosch winemakers.
za-breedekloof.terroir: Alluvial valley soils on a bed of river stones; varied mesoclimates in side valleys.

za-buffeljags.name: Buffeljags
za-buffeljags.summary: A ward around the Buffeljags River and dam east of Swellendam. It sits in warm, dry country along the lower Breede River system, between the Robertson valley and the coast, and most of its grapes are sold in bulk.

za-calitzdorp.name: Calitzdorp
za-calitzdorp.grapes: Touriga Nacional, Tinta Barocca, Souzão, Muscat, Chenin Blanc
za-calitzdorp.summary: A small Klein Karoo town that calls itself South Africa's port capital. The Nel cousins at Boplaas and De Krans, and Axe Hill, make fortified wines from Portuguese varieties in Cape Vintage, Cape Tawny and Cape Ruby styles, the names used since 'port' was retired under the EU agreement in 2012. Hot days, cold nights and low rainfall concentrate the grapes. Its ward is Groenfontein.
za-calitzdorp.terroir: Alluvial and shale soils along the Gamka River; about 200 to 300 mm of rain.

za-cango-valley.name: Cango Valley
za-cango-valley.summary: A ward north of Oudtshoorn in the valley of the Cango Caves. It lies in the hot Oudtshoorn ostrich country.

za-cape-agulhas.name: Cape Agulhas
za-cape-agulhas.summary: The district at Africa's southern tip; almost all its vines are in the Elim ward. Strong winds and a cool ripening season produce pungent Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon.

za-cape-coast.name: Cape Coast
za-cape-coast.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir
za-cape-coast.summary: An overarching region that combines the Coastal Region and Cape South Coast, allowing blends of, say, Stellenbosch and Elgin fruit to name a coastal origin. It is a recent addition to the Wine of Origin hierarchy, sitting between the Western Cape unit and the regions.

za-cape-south-coast.name: Cape South Coast
za-cape-south-coast.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Shiraz
za-cape-south-coast.summary: The cool southern coastal region from Elgin to Plettenberg Bay, home to Walker Bay and its Hemel-en-Aarde wards, Elim and Elgin. Most of its vineyards are young, planted from the 1970s onward, and it is South Africa's main source of Pinot Noir.

za-cape-town.name: Cape Town
za-cape-town.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Muscat de Frontignan
za-cape-town.summary: A district named after the city, combining the wards of Constantia, Durbanville, Hout Bay and Philadelphia and the vineyards of the Cape Peninsula, including Cape Point. At its farthest point it is 36 km from the city centre. It replaced the former Cape Point and Tygerberg districts, which no longer appear on the February 2026 list.
za-cape-town.terroir: Sea on three sides, Table Mountain sandstone and granite, and the cooling south-easter; one of the coolest districts in South Africa.

za-cape-west-coast.name: Cape West Coast
za-cape-west-coast.summary: A subregion grouping the Atlantic-facing Darling and Lutzville Valley districts, St Helena Bay and the Bamboes Bay and Lamberts Bay wards, all cooled by the Benguela current. It was proposed in 2019 and appears on the February 2026 list of production areas.

za-cederberg.name: Cederberg
za-cederberg.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Chardonnay
za-cederberg.summary: A stand-alone ward in the Cederberg wilderness, with some of South Africa's highest and remotest vineyards at about 950 to 1,100 m. The Nieuwoudt family's Cederberg Private Cellar at Dwarsrivier, planted in the 1970s, makes crisp Sauvignon, Chenin and Shiraz.
za-cederberg.terroir: Sandy soils from Table Mountain sandstone; cold winters with snow, hot dry summers.

za-central-drakensberg.name: Central Drakensberg
za-central-drakensberg.summary: A district in the foothills of the Drakensberg near Winterton. Its vineyards at about 1,000 m face summer rainfall and hail.

za-central-orange-river.name: Central Orange River
za-central-orange-river.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Colombard, Muscat d'Alexandrie, Pinotage, Shiraz
za-central-orange-river.summary: The most northerly winegrowing area of the Cape, along about 350 km of the Orange River around Upington, Keimoes and Kakamas. Changed from a ward to a district after a 2019 proposal, it has five wards. About 6,000 ha are planted, largely for white wine, using high hut, gable and T-trellises that shade the grapes; vineyards on river islands are cooled by the water.
za-central-orange-river.terroir: Alluvial river soils; very hot and arid, fully irrigated.

za-ceres.name: Ceres
za-ceres.summary: A ward in the Ceres valley and plateau, high and cold in winter. Its high, cool vineyards produce Chenin Blanc and Sauvignon Blanc prized for freshness, and the district is otherwise known for apples and pears.

za-ceres-plateau.name: Ceres Plateau
za-ceres-plateau.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir
za-ceres-plateau.summary: A high plateau north-east of Ceres at about 1,000 m, apple and pear country whose cool vineyards supply sought-after Chenin and Pinot to Cape producers. It is one of the coldest wine districts in the Western Cape, with snow in winter.

za-citrusdal-mountain.name: Citrusdal Mountain
za-citrusdal-mountain.summary: The mountain district above the Citrusdal valley, whose old, dry-farmed bush vines on sandstone are among the most prized in the new South Africa. Its ward is Piekenierskloof, and its high Skurfberg vineyards supply Chenin to Sadie, Alheit and others.
za-citrusdal-mountain.terroir: Sandy, Table Mountain sandstone soils at up to 1,000 m; dry and hot by day, cold at night.

za-citrusdal-valley.name: Citrusdal Valley
za-citrusdal-valley.summary: The citrus-growing southern Olifants River valley around Citrusdal and Clanwilliam, irrigated from the Clanwilliam Dam. Its irrigated vineyards supply large cellars; the old dry-farmed vines that excite new-wave producers are in the mountains above.

za-coastal-region.name: Coastal Region
za-coastal-region.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Pinotage, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc
za-coastal-region.summary: The Coastal Region includes South Africa's best-known districts: Cape Town, Stellenbosch, Paarl, Franschhoek, Wellington, Swartland, Tulbagh, Darling and Lutzville Valley. 'WO Coastal Region' usually indicates a blend across several of them.

za-constantia.name: Constantia
za-constantia.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Muscat de Frontignan
za-constantia.summary:
Constantia is the cradle of Cape wine and the source of one of history's most famous sweet wines. Simon van der Stel was granted the land in 1685 and planted a large vineyard on the eastern slopes of the Constantiaberg; after his death in 1712 the estate was split into Groot Constantia, Klein Constantia and Bergvliet. From 1778 Hendrik Cloete made an unfortified wine from late-picked Muscat de Frontignan (with some Pontac, Muscadel and Chenin) that European kings, Napoleon on St Helena, Jane Austen's characters and Baudelaire's verse all celebrated. Phylloxera and the end of imperial preference ended it in the late nineteenth century; Klein Constantia revived it as Vin de Constance in 1986, followed by Groot Constantia (Grand Constance) and Buitenverwachting.

Today the ward's handful of estates, now surrounded by expensive suburbs, make some of South Africa's best Sauvignon Blanc and Sauvignon-Sémillon blends, aided by sea air from False Bay a few kilometres away. The ward also carries a modern history: under the Group Areas Act, Constantia was declared a white area in 1961 and families of colour were forcibly removed; the Solomon family won back its land through a restitution claim in 2010.
za-constantia.terroir: East- and south-east-facing slopes of the Constantiaberg on decomposed granite and sandstone, about 1,000 mm of rain a year, and a mean February temperature of about 20.6 degrees C; cool sea breezes from False Bay.
za-constantia.nerd_note: Klein Constantia's Vin de Constance bottle reproduces a squat, hand-blown 18th-century design, and it is aged about four years before release.

za-darling.name: Darling
za-darling.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Pinotage, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-darling.summary: Darling, an hour north of Cape Town on the west coast, is famous for spring wild flowers and for cool Sauvignon Blanc. Its Groenekloof ward is one of the closest in South Africa to the cold Atlantic.
za-darling.terroir: Decomposed granite hills catching Atlantic fog and wind.

za-devon-valley.name: Devon Valley
za-devon-valley.grapes: Merlot, Pinotage, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc
za-devon-valley.summary: A small, sheltered valley north-west of Stellenbosch town between the Bottelary Hills and Papegaaiberg, known for Merlot and Pinotage on granite and shale soils. It is one of the most sheltered parts of the district, and its small size keeps it a district of family estates.

za-douglas.name: Douglas
za-douglas.summary: A district around Douglas, near the confluence of the Orange and Vaal rivers, with irrigated vineyards. Like the Central Orange River vineyards, it depends on irrigation in a hot, arid climate.

za-durbanville.name: Durbanville
za-durbanville.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Pinotage
za-durbanville.summary: Rolling wheat-and-vine country on the northern edge of Cape Town, whose hills catch Atlantic breezes and night-time mist. Durbanville made its name for pungent, green-fruited Sauvignon Blanc and soft Merlot, and many farms (Diemersdal, Meerendal, Altydgedacht) have been in the same families for generations.
za-durbanville.terroir: Deep, red, decomposed granite and shale soils that hold water, allowing dry farming; vineyards up to about 380 m.

za-eastern-cape.name: Eastern Cape
za-eastern-cape.summary: The Eastern Cape was designated a geographical unit in 2009. Its only ward is St Francis Bay, on the coast west of Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha). Its few vineyards face rain spread through the year, unlike the Western Cape's dry summers.

za-eilandia.name: Eilandia
za-eilandia.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-eilandia.summary: A ward on low-lying land along the Breede River between Robertson and Ashton. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

za-elandskloof-kaaimansgat.name: Elandskloof/Kaaimansgat
za-elandskloof-kaaimansgat.summary: A high, cool ward in the mountains near Villiersdorp. Bouchard Finlayson's Kaaimansgat ('crocodile's lair') Chardonnay comes from vineyards here at around 700 m. It is one of the coolest Chardonnay sites in the Cape.

za-elgin.name: Elgin
za-elgin.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Riesling, Shiraz
za-elgin.summary: Elgin is a high basin about an hour east of Cape Town, ringed by the Hottentots Holland mountains, which grew most of South Africa's apples before its farmers began planting vines in the late 1980s. Its altitude (200 to 800 m), cloud and proximity to the sea make it one of the coolest districts in South Africa, and its Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir are taut and fine. Paul Cluver, Oak Valley, Iona, Richard Kershaw and Shannon lead.
za-elgin.terroir: Table Mountain sandstone and Bokkeveld shale; cool summers, about 1,000 mm of rain.

za-elim.name: Elim
za-elim.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon, Shiraz, Pinot Noir
za-elim.summary: Elim's vineyards lie near Cape Agulhas, Africa's southernmost point, around the Moravian mission village of Elim, founded in 1824 and a national monument. Strong summer winds and a very cool ripening season give pungent, mineral Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon and peppery Shiraz.
za-elim.terroir: Ferricrete, shale and sandstone soils; constant wind off the sea.

za-franschhoek.name: Franschhoek
za-franschhoek.grapes: Sémillon, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chenin Blanc, Pinot Noir
za-franschhoek.summary: Franschhoek, the 'French corner', is the valley where the VOC settled Huguenot refugees after 1688. It is enclosed on three sides by the Groot Drakenstein and Franschhoek mountains, with the Berg River rising at its head. The district holds some of South Africa's oldest vineyards, including Sémillon (and the rare Sémillon Gris) planted in the early twentieth century, and it is a centre of Cap Classique and of the Cape's restaurant culture. The Huguenot Monument (1948) stands at the head of the town.
za-franschhoek.terroir: Sandy alluvium on the valley floor and decomposed sandstone and granite on the slopes; enclosed, warmer by day and colder at night than Stellenbosch, with snow on the peaks in winter.
za-franschhoek.nerd_note: Boekenhoutskloof's Sémillon comes from vines planted in 1902 and 1942, among the oldest Sémillon in the world.

za-free-state.name: Free State
za-free-state.summary: The Free State geographical unit has one ward, Rietrivier FS, on the Riet River near Jacobsdal. Grapes there are mostly grown for local co-operative wine and brandy.

za-goedemoed.name: Goedemoed
za-goedemoed.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-goedemoed.summary: A ward of the Robertson district. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

za-goree.name: Goree
za-goree.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-goree.summary: A ward west of Robertson town. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

za-goudini.name: Goudini
za-goudini.summary: A ward around Rawsonville in the Breedekloof. Its alluvial soils over river stones and the cooling effect of the surrounding mountains suit Chenin Blanc and Colombard, delivered mostly to the Goudini co-operative cellar.

za-goudmyn.name: Goudmyn
za-goudmyn.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-goudmyn.summary: A ward of the Robertson district. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

za-goukou-river-valley.name: Goukou River Valley
za-goukou-river-valley.summary: A ward along the Goukou River inland from Stilbaai. It is one of the most easterly coastal wine wards on the Garden Route, with a mild, wet maritime climate.

za-greater-cape.name: Greater Cape
za-greater-cape.summary: An overarching unit created after a 2019 proposal that groups the Western Cape, Northern Cape and Eastern Cape geographical units, so that wines blended across provincial lines (for example Western Cape and Orange River fruit) can carry a Cape origin.

za-greyton.name: Greyton
za-greyton.summary: A ward around the village of Greyton below the Riviersonderend mountains, where Samantha O'Keefe's Lismore Estate makes Chardonnay and Syrah. Its vineyards are cool and wind-exposed.

za-groblershoop.name: Groblershoop
za-groblershoop.summary: A ward on the Orange River around the town of Groblershoop in the Central Orange River district, an irrigated desert-oasis vineyard area. The Orange River vineyards ripen very early (harvest can start in December), and most grapes go to Orange River Cellars, one of the largest wine businesses in South Africa, for Colombard, Chenin Blanc, sweet Muscat and juice.

za-groenberg.name: Groenberg
za-groenberg.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-groenberg.summary: A ward around the Groenberg hill north of Wellington town, with granite soils. It is one of five Wellington wards on the February 2026 Wine of Origin list; most producers still label their wine WO Wellington.

za-groenekloof.name: Groenekloof
za-groenekloof.summary: The Darling ward nearest the Atlantic, whose Sauvignon Blanc, cooled by sea breezes and fog, spearheaded the area's development. Groote Post's Peter Pentz farms here. Neil Ellis was an early buyer of its cool-climate fruit.
za-groenekloof.terroir: Granite-derived soils on hills a few kilometres from the sea.

za-groenfontein.name: Groenfontein
za-groenfontein.summary: A ward in the Groenfontein valley north of Calitzdorp, below the Swartberg. Its vineyards supply Calitzdorp's port-style producers with Touriga Nacional, Tinta Barocca and Muscat, ripened in a hot, dry valley enclosed by mountains.

za-grootdrink.name: Grootdrink
za-grootdrink.summary: A ward on the Orange River around the town of Grootdrink in the Central Orange River district, an irrigated desert-oasis vineyard area. The Orange River vineyards ripen very early (harvest can start in December), and most grapes go to Orange River Cellars, one of the largest wine businesses in South Africa, for Colombard, Chenin Blanc, sweet Muscat and juice.

za-hartswater.name: Hartswater
za-hartswater.summary: A ward in the Vaalharts irrigation scheme in the far north of the Northern Cape. The scheme, one of the largest in the southern hemisphere, grows grain, pecans and grapes.

za-hemel-en-aarde-ridge.name: Hemel-en-Aarde Ridge
za-hemel-en-aarde-ridge.summary: The highest and furthest inland of the three Hemel-en-Aarde wards, at the top of the valley around 300 m and above, with cooler nights. Creation and Domaine des Dieux are here, and Chris and Suzaan Alheit's Hemelrand farm is nearby.
za-hemel-en-aarde-ridge.terroir: Shale and sandstone with some granite; cool and windy.

za-hemel-en-aarde-valley.name: Hemel-en-Aarde Valley
za-hemel-en-aarde-valley.grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Pinotage, Sauvignon Blanc
za-hemel-en-aarde-valley.summary: The lowest of the three Hemel-en-Aarde wards, closest to the sea at Hermanus. Hamilton Russell Vineyards (1975) and Bouchard Finlayson (1989, a venture between Peter Finlayson and Burgundy's Paul Bouchard) established South African Pinot Noir and Chardonnay here; the clay-rich shale soils give wines of structure and minerality.
za-hemel-en-aarde-valley.terroir: Bokkeveld shale with high clay content, stony; cool sea breezes, about 750 mm of rain.

za-herbertsdale.name: Herbertsdale
za-herbertsdale.summary: A stand-alone ward near the village of Herbertsdale inland from Mossel Bay. Its mild Garden Route climate, with rain through the year, suits white varieties such as Sauvignon Blanc.

za-hex-river-valley.name: Hex River Valley
za-hex-river-valley.summary: The Hex River Valley around De Doorns, South Africa's largest table-grape area, also grows wine grapes. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy.

za-hoopsrivier.name: Hoopsrivier
za-hoopsrivier.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-hoopsrivier.summary: A ward of the Robertson district. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

za-hout-bay.name: Hout Bay
za-hout-bay.summary: One of South Africa's smallest wards, in the steep valley behind Hout Bay harbour on the Cape Peninsula, with a few hectares of vines. Its vines grow on steep slopes in sight of the Atlantic.
za-hout-bay.terroir: Steep granite and sandstone slopes facing the Atlantic.

za-jonkershoek-valley.name: Jonkershoek Valley
za-jonkershoek-valley.summary: A narrow, steep-sided valley running south-east from Stellenbosch town into the Jonkershoek mountains, one of the wettest and most enclosed parts of the district. Morning shade and late sun give long, slow ripening; Stark-Condé and Neil Ellis's Jonkershoek vineyards make fine, fresh Cabernet.
za-jonkershoek-valley.terroir: Decomposed granite and sandstone colluvium on steep slopes; about 1,000 mm or more of rain.

za-kakamas.name: Kakamas
za-kakamas.summary: A ward on the Orange River around the town of Kakamas in the Central Orange River district, an irrigated desert-oasis vineyard area. The Orange River vineyards ripen very early (harvest can start in December), and most grapes go to Orange River Cellars, one of the largest wine businesses in South Africa, for Colombard, Chenin Blanc, sweet Muscat and juice.

za-karoo-hoogland.name: Karoo-Hoogland
za-karoo-hoogland.summary: A high-plateau region in the Northern Cape whose only district is Sutherland-Karoo, around one of South Africa's coldest towns. Its vineyards, at around 1,500 m, are the highest in South Africa.

za-keeromsberg.name: Keeromsberg
za-keeromsberg.summary: A ward named after the Keeromsberg mountain north of Worcester. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy. Grapes from here go mainly to the Worcester district's co-operatives and to the brandy distilleries that make Worcester South Africa's brandy capital; ward names are rarely used on bottles.

za-keimoes.name: Keimoes
za-keimoes.summary: A ward on the Orange River around the town of Keimoes in the Central Orange River district, an irrigated desert-oasis vineyard area. The Orange River vineyards ripen very early (harvest can start in December), and most grapes go to Orange River Cellars, one of the largest wine businesses in South Africa, for Colombard, Chenin Blanc, sweet Muscat and juice.

za-klaasvoogds.name: Klaasvoogds
za-klaasvoogds.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-klaasvoogds.summary: A ward in the foothills of the Langeberg north-east of Robertson. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

za-klein-karoo.name: Klein Karoo
za-klein-karoo.grapes: Muscat, Touriga Nacional, Chenin Blanc, Colombard
za-klein-karoo.summary: The semi-arid valley along Route 62 from Montagu to the Langkloof, known for Calitzdorp's fortified wines, Muscadel and potstill brandy. Vines grow in kloofs and river valleys between ostrich farms.

za-klein-river.name: Klein River
za-klein-river.summary: A ward near Stanford along the Klein River, where award-winning wines (Raka) have emerged. Its cool coastal climate suits Sauvignon Blanc and Bordeaux varieties.

za-koekenaap.name: Koekenaap
za-koekenaap.summary: A cool, sea-influenced ward close to the Atlantic in the Lutzville Valley, where grapes ripen slowly in coastal fog. It is one of the most northerly coastal wards in South Africa.

za-koo-plateau.name: Koo Plateau
za-koo-plateau.summary: A high plateau north of Montagu at about 1,000 m, apple and pear country with a cool climate. Its cool upland climate attracts winemakers looking for fresh Chenin Blanc.

za-kwazulu-natal.name: KwaZulu-Natal
za-kwazulu-natal.grapes: Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay
za-kwazulu-natal.summary: KwaZulu-Natal, designated in 2005, stretches from Greytown to the Midlands at up to about 1,500 m. Its summer rainfall makes viticulture difficult; it contains the Lions River and Central Drakensberg districts.

za-kweekvallei.name: Kweekvallei
za-kweekvallei.summary: A small ward near Prince Albert in the Karoo. Its irrigated vineyards grow small quantities of Shiraz and other reds in a hot, dry climate at the foot of the Swartberg mountains.

za-lamberts-bay.name: Lamberts Bay
za-lamberts-bay.summary: A coastal ward around the fishing town of Lamberts Bay, cooled by the Benguela current. Its vineyards, among the coolest on the west coast, mostly grow Sauvignon Blanc.

za-langeberg-garcia.name: Langeberg-Garcia
za-langeberg-garcia.summary: A district along the Langeberg range around the Garcia Pass near Riversdale. Its few vineyards lie at the eastern end of the Langeberg, on the edge of the Klein Karoo, with a cooler, wetter climate than the valleys to the north.

za-lanseria.name: Lanseria
za-lanseria.summary: A ward near Lanseria, north-west of Johannesburg in Gauteng, listed under no geographical unit on the February 2026 schedule; it is one of the few demarcated wine areas in South Africa's interior highveld.

za-le-chasseur.name: Le Chasseur
za-le-chasseur.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-le-chasseur.summary: A ward of the Robertson district north of the town. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

za-leipoldtville-sandveld.name: Leipoldtville-Sandveld
za-leipoldtville-sandveld.summary: A ward in the sandy coastal plain (Sandveld) around Leipoldtville, west of Clanwilliam. Its sandy soils and cool Atlantic influence suit Sauvignon Blanc and Chenin Blanc.

za-limietberg.name: Limietberg
za-limietberg.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-limietberg.summary: A ward on the lower slopes of the Limietberg (Hawequa) range east of Wellington, where mountain foothills create cooler mesoclimates. It is one of five Wellington wards on the February 2026 Wine of Origin list; most producers still label their wine WO Wellington.

za-limpopo.name: Limpopo
za-limpopo.summary: A geographical unit covering South Africa's northernmost province; it has no regions, districts or wards on the February 2026 list. Summer rainfall and subtropical heat make viticulture marginal.

za-lions-river.name: Lions River
za-lions-river.summary: A district in the KwaZulu-Natal Midlands near Howick, at about 1,000 to 1,200 m. Summer rainfall makes viticulture challenging, but cool nights suit Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay.

za-lower-duivenhoks-river.name: Lower Duivenhoks River
za-lower-duivenhoks-river.summary: A small district along the lower Duivenhoks River between Heidelberg and the coast at Witsand. Its few vineyards benefit from sea breezes off the Indian Ocean near Witsand.

za-lutzville-valley.name: Lutzville Valley
za-lutzville-valley.summary: A district near the mouth of the Olifants River with large irrigated vineyards, including the Lutzville co-operative. It is one of the most northerly coastal wine districts in South Africa, cooled by the Atlantic and dependent on irrigation from the Olifants River.

za-malgas.name: Malgas
za-malgas.grapes: Syrah, Mourvèdre, Touriga Nacional, Chenin Blanc
za-malgas.summary: A pioneering ward on a stony plateau 80 km east of Cape Agulhas, about 70 m above the Breede River. David and Rita Trafford's Sijnn planted drought-tolerant Mediterranean varieties here; rainfall is only about 350 mm, moderated by sea breezes from the coast 15 km away.
za-malgas.terroir: Complex stony soils of shale and quartzite gravel.

za-malmesbury.name: Malmesbury
za-malmesbury.summary: The ward around Malmesbury, the Swartland's main town, among wheatfields on Malmesbury shale. Its old dryland bush vines of Chenin Blanc and Pinotage were long sold to the Swartland Winery co-operative and are now sought by smaller producers too.

za-mcgregor.name: McGregor
za-mcgregor.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-mcgregor.summary: A ward around the village of McGregor, south of Robertson below the Riviersonderend mountains, cooler and drier than the valley floor. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate.

za-mid-berg-river.name: Mid-Berg River
za-mid-berg-river.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-mid-berg-river.summary: A ward on the alluvial terraces of the middle Berg River between Wellington and Paarl. It is one of five Wellington wards on the February 2026 Wine of Origin list; most producers still label their wine WO Wellington.

za-montagu.name: Montagu
za-montagu.summary: A ward around the spa town of Montagu at the western gateway of the Klein Karoo, famous for its fortified Muscadel. Its Muscadel is made from red and white Muscat à Petits Grains, fortified to sweetness.

za-moordkuil.name: Moordkuil
za-moordkuil.summary: A ward of the Worcester district. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy. Grapes from here go mainly to the Worcester district's co-operatives and to the brandy distilleries that make Worcester South Africa's brandy capital; ward names are rarely used on bottles.

za-napier.name: Napier
za-napier.summary: A stand-alone ward around the Overberg village of Napier, between Bredasdorp and Caledon. Like nearby Elim, it is cooled by winds off the sea near Africa's southern tip, which suits Sauvignon Blanc and Shiraz.

za-nieuwoudtville.name: Nieuwoudtville
za-nieuwoudtville.summary: A ward around the town of Nieuwoudtville on the Bokkeveld plateau, known for spring wild flowers, at the north-western edge of the Cape. Its vineyards are cool and high, at about 750 m.

za-north-west.name: North West
za-north-west.summary: A geographical unit covering the North West province; it has no regions, districts or wards on the February 2026 list. Summer rainfall and highveld frost make viticulture marginal.

za-northern-cape.name: Northern Cape
za-northern-cape.grapes: Colombard, Chenin Blanc, Muscat d'Alexandrie, Pinotage
za-northern-cape.summary: The Northern Cape geographical unit covers the irrigated vineyards of the Orange River and the high Karoo around Sutherland. Most fruit goes to large co-operative cellars. Its best-known wine area is the Central Orange River district around Upington, where vineyards on islands in the river are cooled by the water.

za-nuveld-karoo.name: Nuveld-Karoo
za-nuveld-karoo.summary: A district on the high Karoo plateau inland of the Cape fold mountains, listed on the February 2026 schedule with no wards. Its vineyards are among the most remote in South Africa.

za-nuy.name: Nuy
za-nuy.summary: A small valley east of Worcester whose Nuy cellar is famous for fortified Muscadel. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy.

za-olifants-river.name: Olifants River
za-olifants-river.summary: The region along the Olifants River from Citrusdal to Lutzville, with old mountain vineyards at Piekenierskloof and large irrigated cellars at Vredendal. It is citrus and rooibos country.

za-outeniqua.name: Outeniqua
za-outeniqua.summary: A ward in the Outeniqua mountains north of George, where vineyards on the Montagu Pass reach about 700 m. Its vineyards near George get rain through the year and cooler temperatures than the Klein Karoo valleys to the north.

za-overberg.name: Overberg
za-overberg.summary: A broad district of wheatfields and mountains east of Elgin, with wards at Elandskloof/Kaaimansgat, Greyton, Klein River, Shaw's Mountain and Theewater. Its cool, high wards produce Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc.

za-paardeberg-perdeberg.name: Paardeberg/Perdeberg
za-paardeberg-perdeberg.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Grenache, Cinsault, Mourvèdre
za-paardeberg-perdeberg.summary: The granite massif of the Paardeberg (Perdeberg in Afrikaans), on the border of the Swartland and Paarl, is the spiritual home of the Swartland revival. Eben Sadie's farm and cellar, A.A. Badenhorst's Kalmoesfontein and many old Chenin and Cinsault vineyards are here. Its decomposed granite holds winter rain, so old bush vines survive without irrigation.
za-paardeberg-perdeberg.terroir: Decomposed granite over clay on rounded hills; warm, dry and windy.

za-paardeberg-south.name: Paardeberg South
za-paardeberg-south.summary: The southern foothills of the Paardeberg, separated as their own ward, with granite soils similar to the main Paardeberg ward. Old dry-farmed bush vines of Chenin Blanc and Cinsault here supply several new-wave Swartland labels.

za-paarl.name: Paarl
za-paarl.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Shiraz, Pinotage, Chenin Blanc, Chardonnay
za-paarl.summary: Paarl, named after the pearl-like granite domes of Paarl Mountain, lies north of Stellenbosch along the Berg River. It was the seat of the KWV from 1918, which made it the administrative capital of the industry for most of the twentieth century, and home to Nederburg, whose annual auction (from 1975) became the country's most important wine sale. The district is warmer than Stellenbosch and its Shiraz, Cabernet, Pinotage and Chenin are generous and ripe. Its wards are Simonsberg-Paarl, Voor-Paardeberg and Agter-Paarl.
za-paarl.terroir: Granite domes and slopes, with alluvial soils along the Berg River; the valley needs supplementary irrigation in hot summers while the eastern slopes hold water.

za-papegaaiberg.name: Papegaaiberg
za-papegaaiberg.summary: A small hill just west of Stellenbosch town, the 'parrot mountain' where early settlers practised shooting at a wooden parrot. The Bergkelder, Distell's (now Heineken Beverages') maturation cellar, is tunnelled into its slopes.
za-papegaaiberg.terroir: Granite and shale on a low ridge.

za-philadelphia.name: Philadelphia
za-philadelphia.summary: A small ward north of Durbanville around the village of Philadelphia, on hills up to about 260 m within sight of the Atlantic, known for structured Bordeaux-style reds. Capaia, with its hilltop winery, is the ward's best-known estate.
za-philadelphia.terroir: Weathered shale and granite; cool Atlantic influence with large day-night differences.

za-piekenierskloof.name: Piekenierskloof
za-piekenierskloof.grapes: Grenache, Chenin Blanc, Palomino, Pinotage, Cinsault
za-piekenierskloof.summary: A high plateau above the Piekenierskloof Pass south of Citrusdal, with some of South Africa's oldest Grenache and Palomino vineyards. Dry-farmed bush vines on deep sand give perfumed, light-coloured Grenache and textured whites prized by Swartland and Stellenbosch winemakers.
za-piekenierskloof.terroir: Deep, sandy soils derived from sandstone at 600 to 750 m.

za-piket-bo-berg.name: Piket-Bo-Berg
za-piket-bo-berg.summary: A high plateau on top of the Piketberg mountain, north of the Swartland at about 600 to 700 m, cooler than the valleys below; the WOSA text calls it Piketberg-Bo-Berg.

za-plettenberg-bay.name: Plettenberg Bay
za-plettenberg-bay.summary: The newest and furthest-east district on the Cape South Coast, in mountainous terrain about 20 km east of Plettenberg Bay. The first vines were planted in 2000 (Bramon, known for Cap Classique). Cool coastal climate and high-carbon soils suit Sauvignon Blanc and sparkling.

za-polkadraai-hills.name: Polkadraai Hills
za-polkadraai-hills.grapes: Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc
za-polkadraai-hills.summary: Hills west of Stellenbosch near the R310 and Polkadraai Road, open to cool breezes from both False Bay and the Atlantic. Johan Reyneke farms biodynamically here, and the ward's sandy granite soils give fresh, fragrant Syrah and Chenin.
za-polkadraai-hills.terroir: Sandy, decomposed granite over clay at about 100 to 300 m.

za-porseleinberg.name: Porseleinberg
za-porseleinberg.summary: A ward named after the 'porcelain mountain' between Riebeek-Kasteel and the Berg River, whose blue-grey schist soils Boekenhoutskloof chose for its Porseleinberg Syrah, farmed organically by Callie Louw since the first vintage in 2010.
za-porseleinberg.terroir: Malmesbury schist with very little topsoil; warm and dry.

za-prieska.name: Prieska
za-prieska.summary: A ward around Prieska on the Orange River. Its hot, dry vineyards are irrigated from the river and grow mainly white grapes for local cellars.

za-prince-albert.name: Prince Albert
za-prince-albert.summary: A district around the Karoo town of Prince Albert below the Swartberg, with the wards Kweekvallei, Prince Albert Valley and Swartberg. Its few vineyards make small volumes for local producers.

za-prince-albert-valley.name: Prince Albert Valley
za-prince-albert-valley.summary: A ward in the valley around Prince Albert, a hot, dry Karoo town at the foot of the Swartberg Pass. Its few hectares of vines are irrigated from mountain streams.

za-riebeekberg.name: Riebeekberg
za-riebeekberg.summary: The slopes of the Kasteelberg around the villages of Riebeek-Kasteel and Riebeek-West, where the Mullineuxs farm their Roundstone vineyard on schist and iron-rich soils. Many of the Swartland's new-wave producers source fruit here.

za-riebeeksrivier.name: Riebeeksrivier
za-riebeeksrivier.summary: A newer ward along the Riebeeks River valley below the Kasteelberg, on shale and alluvial soils. It lies between the Riebeekberg and Porseleinberg wards in the heart of the new-wave Swartland.

za-rietrivier-fs.name: Rietrivier FS
za-rietrivier-fs.summary: A ward on the Riet River near Jacobsdal in the Free State, home of the Landzicht cellar. It is one of the few demarcated wine areas in South Africa's interior.

za-robertson.name: Robertson
za-robertson.grapes: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Colombard, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon, Muscadel
za-robertson.summary: The 'valley of vines and roses' along the Breede River is the only part of the Cape with significant lime-rich soils, which also suit its many racehorse studs. Hot summers are tempered by south-easterly winds that bring moist air up the valley. Danie de Wet of De Wetshof pioneered Chardonnay here in the 1970s, and Graham Beck's Madeba farm built South Africa's leading Cap Classique house in the 1990s. The district has 14 wards.
za-robertson.terroir: Calcareous soils over limestone along the Breede, with alluvium; about 400 mm of rain, irrigation needed.

za-rooikrans.name: Rooikrans
za-rooikrans.summary: A ward of the Worcester district. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy. Grapes from here go mainly to the Worcester district's co-operatives and to the brandy distilleries that make Worcester South Africa's brandy capital; ward names are rarely used on bottles.

za-scherpenheuvel.name: Scherpenheuvel
za-scherpenheuvel.summary: A ward on the road between Worcester and Robertson near the Brandvlei Dam. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy.

za-shaws-mountain.name: Shaw's Mountain
za-shaws-mountain.summary: A recently added Overberg ward on the mountain slopes between Caledon and the Hemel-en-Aarde. Its cool, elevated slopes are suited to Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay.

za-simonsberg-paarl.name: Simonsberg-Paarl
za-simonsberg-paarl.summary: The north-eastern slopes of the Simonsberg facing Paarl, on decomposed granite. Glen Carlou, Plaisir de Merle, Backsberg and Rupert & Rothschild make Bordeaux blends and Chardonnay here. It is warmer than the Simonsberg-Stellenbosch side of the mountain, and its reds are correspondingly riper.
za-simonsberg-paarl.terroir: Granite-derived soils on north- and east-facing slopes; warmer than the Stellenbosch side of the mountain.

za-simonsberg-stellenbosch.name: Simonsberg-Stellenbosch
za-simonsberg-stellenbosch.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinotage, Merlot, Shiraz, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
za-simonsberg-stellenbosch.summary: The southern and western slopes of the granite Simonsberg (1,390 m) north-east of Stellenbosch, one of the most prestigious wards in South Africa and among the first to be demarcated. Its well-drained, red decomposed-granite soils, altitude and afternoon sea breezes give structured, long-lived Cabernet and Bordeaux blends and the country's most famous Pinotage. Kanonkop, Rustenberg, Thelema, Tokara, Warwick, Delheim and Uitkyk are all here.
za-simonsberg-stellenbosch.terroir: Decomposed granite (red Hutton and Clovelly soils) at about 150 to 500 m; south- and west-facing slopes catch the False Bay breeze.
za-simonsberg-stellenbosch.nerd_note: The official schedule of February 2026 misspells the ward as 'Simonsberg-Stellenbosh'.

za-slanghoek.name: Slanghoek
za-slanghoek.summary: The Slanghoek valley north-west of Rawsonville, under the Slanghoek mountains. The Slanghoek cellar, a former co-operative, makes the ward's best-known wines, including fortified Hanepoot (Muscat d'Alexandrie) and Chenin Blanc.

za-springfontein-rim.name: Springfontein Rim
za-springfontein-rim.summary: A small coastal ward near Stanford around the Springfontein estate, close to the sea on limestone-influenced soils. The Springfontein estate, owned by a German family, grows Chenin Blanc and Pinotage on limestone-influenced coastal soils there.

za-spruitdrift.name: Spruitdrift
za-spruitdrift.summary: An irrigated ward on the lower Olifants River near Vredendal. Its grapes go mostly to the large Namaqua Wines cellar, for inexpensive whites and reds, and the hot, dry valley floor depends on irrigation from the Clanwilliam Dam.

za-st-francis-bay.name: St Francis Bay
za-st-francis-bay.summary: The Eastern Cape's only ward, near the coastal resort of St Francis Bay. Its cool maritime climate suits Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir.

za-st-helena-bay.name: St Helena Bay
za-st-helena-bay.summary: A coastal ward on St Helena Bay on the Atlantic, the fishing coast north of Saldanha, now grouped in the Cape West Coast subregion though listed under the Swartland district.
za-st-helena-bay.terroir: Sandy soils, cold Benguela fog and wind.

za-stanford-foothills.name: Stanford Foothills
za-stanford-foothills.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc, Pinot Noir
za-stanford-foothills.summary: A ward on the foothills of the Kleinrivier mountains above the village of Stanford, east of the Hemel-en-Aarde. It was registered as a ward recently, alongside Springfontein Rim and Sunday's Glen, as Walker Bay's vineyards spread east from the Hemel-en-Aarde.

za-stellenbosch.name: Stellenbosch
za-stellenbosch.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Shiraz, Merlot, Pinotage, Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc
za-stellenbosch.summary:
Stellenbosch is South Africa's most famous wine district and its intellectual centre. The town, founded by Simon van der Stel in 1679 and shaded by oaks, has the country's only university degree in viticulture and oenology, the Elsenburg agricultural college and the Nietvoorbij research institute. More than 200 producers farm the district's slopes, from historic estates to modern wineries.

Its strength is red wine, above all Cabernet Sauvignon and Bordeaux-style blends, which gain structure and freshness from the district's granite mountains and the cooling south-easter off False Bay. Meerlust Rubicon (first made in 1980), Kanonkop Paul Sauer, Vergelegen V and Rust en Vrede's estate blend are classics, and Kanonkop's Pinotage, from vines planted in the 1950s, is the reference for the country's own grape. Old-vine Chenin Blanc from the Bottelary and Helderberg areas and Chardonnay from the higher slopes are equally serious.

The district is divided into eight wards: Banghoek, Bottelary, Devon Valley, Jonkershoek Valley, Papegaaiberg, Polkadraai Hills, Simonsberg-Stellenbosch and Vlottenburg. Much of the best-known land, including the Helderberg slopes around Somerset West (Vergelegen, Rust en Vrede, Waterford, Ernie Els), lies outside any ward and is labelled simply 'Stellenbosch'. The Stellenbosch Wine Route, founded in 1971, was South Africa's first.
za-stellenbosch.terroir: Mountains on three sides (Simonsberg, Jonkershoek, Helderberg) and False Bay to the south; about 600 to 800 mm of rain in the valley, more on the mountains. Decomposed granite on the higher slopes, Table Mountain sandstone higher still, and Malmesbury shale and alluvium on the lower ground to the west.
za-stellenbosch.nerd_note: Stellenbosch's oak-lined streets are a result of Van der Stel's order to plant oaks in the 1680s; the university's experimental farm at Welgevallen is where Perold bred Pinotage in 1925.

za-stettyn.name: Stettyn
za-stettyn.summary: A ward in the Stettynskloof west of Worcester, home of the Stettyn cellar. It is one of seven wards in the Worcester district, a warm, irrigated area whose fruit goes largely to wine and brandy.

za-still-bay.name: Still Bay
za-still-bay.summary: A coastal district around Stilbaai on the Garden Route, with the Goukou River Valley ward. Its vineyards, close to the Indian Ocean, are cooled by sea breezes and grow mostly Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir.

za-stormsvlei.name: Stormsvlei
za-stormsvlei.summary: A ward west of Swellendam near the Riviersonderend, on the road between Robertson and the coast. Its vineyards benefit from cool air drifting up the river valley from the coast.

za-sundays-glen.name: Sunday's Glen
za-sundays-glen.summary: The easternmost Walker Bay ward, beyond Stanford, a cool coastal site. Like the other new Walker Bay wards, it relies on the cooling influence of the Atlantic and on Bokkeveld shale and sandstone soils, which suit Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc.

za-sutherland-karoo.name: Sutherland-Karoo
za-sutherland-karoo.summary: A high-altitude, semi-arid district around Sutherland, South Africa's coldest town and home of the national astronomical observatory, with vineyards at about 1,500 m, the highest in the country.
za-sutherland-karoo.terroir: Dolerite and shale soils; extreme cold in winter.

za-swartberg.name: Swartberg
za-swartberg.summary: A ward in the Swartberg mountains above Prince Albert. Its few hectares of vines grow in a dry, high-altitude setting where cold nights preserve acidity.

za-swartland.name: Swartland
za-swartland.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Shiraz, Grenache, Cinsault, Pinotage, Mourvèdre, Palomino
za-swartland.summary:
The Swartland, the 'black land', takes its name from the renosterbos (rhino bush) that once darkened its rolling wheatfields north of Cape Town. For most of its history it grew grain and supplied big co-operatives with high-yielding grapes. That changed when Charles Back of Fairview and Spice Route began buying land here in the late 1990s and a young winemaker, Eben Sadie, found old, dry-farmed bush vines of Chenin Blanc, Grenache, Cinsault and Syrah on the Paardeberg. His Columella (2000) and Palladius (2002) showed what they could do.

A generation followed: Chris and Andrea Mullineux, Adi Badenhorst at Kalmoesfontein, Callie Louw at Porseleinberg, Craig Hawkins (Testalonga), Lammershoek, David and Nadia Sadie, Donovan Rall. Their Swartland Revolution festival (2010 to 2015) and the Swartland Independent Producers association, which sets rules on natural winemaking and regional sourcing, made the district shorthand for South Africa's new wave: whole-bunch Syrah, old-vine Chenin blends aged in old foudres and concrete, and skin-contact whites. The district also has eight wards, from the Paardeberg granite to the schist of the Riebeek and Porseleinberg slopes.
za-swartland.terroir: Warm and dry (400 to 600 mm of rain), with mostly dry-farmed bush vines. Soils include decomposed granite (Paardeberg), Malmesbury shale and schist (Kasteelberg, Porseleinberg) and iron-rich koffieklip.
za-swartland.nerd_note: Sadie's 'Old Vineyard Series' bottles single old vineyards from across the Cape, each label naming the site, such as Skerpioen, Mev. Kirsten and 'T Voetpad.

za-swellendam.name: Swellendam
za-swellendam.summary: A district around the historic town of Swellendam (1743), the third-oldest in South Africa, with wards Buffeljags, Malgas and Stormsvlei. Its warm, dry wards lie along the lower Breede River between Robertson and the coast.

za-theewater.name: Theewater
za-theewater.summary: A ward near the Theewaterskloof Dam and Villiersdorp, at the edge of the Overberg's mountains. The area's growers mainly sell fruit to cellars elsewhere.

za-tradouw.name: Tradouw
za-tradouw.summary: A ward around Barrydale below the Tradouw Pass. Joubert-Tradauw makes Chardonnay and Shiraz here, in one of the Klein Karoo's coolest corners, influenced by air from the coast through the Tradouw Pass.

za-tradouw-highlands.name: Tradouw Highlands
za-tradouw-highlands.summary: A higher, cooler ward in the mountains above Barrydale, whose growers make fresh whites and Pinot Noir. Its vineyards, at about 500 to 600 m, are among the coolest in the Klein Karoo.

za-tulbagh.name: Tulbagh
za-tulbagh.summary: A horseshoe-shaped valley enclosed by the Groot Winterhoek, Witzenberg and Obiekwaberg mountains, about 90 minutes north of Cape Town. Cold air pools on the valley floor at night (a 'cold trap'), giving large day-night temperature swings. Tulbagh's Church Street has 32 national monuments, many restored after the 1969 earthquake. The valley is known for Shiraz and Rhône blends and for Cap Classique pioneer Krone (Twee Jonge Gezellen).
za-tulbagh.terroir: A former lake basin with varied alluvial and sandstone soils.

za-upington.name: Upington
za-upington.summary: A ward on the Orange River around the town of Upington in the Central Orange River district, an irrigated desert-oasis vineyard area. The Orange River vineyards ripen very early (harvest can start in December), and most grapes go to Orange River Cellars, one of the largest wine businesses in South Africa, for Colombard, Chenin Blanc, sweet Muscat and juice.

za-upper-hemel-en-aarde-valley.name: Upper Hemel-en-Aarde Valley
za-upper-hemel-en-aarde-valley.grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Syrah
za-upper-hemel-en-aarde-valley.summary: The middle section of the Hemel-en-Aarde, further inland and slightly warmer, on lighter granite-derived and shale soils. Newton Johnson, La Vierge, Restless River and Storm make some of the country's most elegant Pinot Noir.
za-upper-hemel-en-aarde-valley.terroir: Decomposed granite and shale; more sheltered than the lower valley.

za-upper-langkloof.name: Upper Langkloof
za-upper-langkloof.summary: A high, cool ward in the apple-growing Langkloof valley around Haarlem in the far east of the Klein Karoo. Its cool climate suits Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc.

za-vinkrivier.name: Vinkrivier
za-vinkrivier.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-vinkrivier.summary: A ward along the Vink River near McGregor. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

za-vlottenburg.name: Vlottenburg
za-vlottenburg.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc
za-vlottenburg.summary: A ward south-west of Stellenbosch town around the Vlottenburg railway halt and the Eerste River, where cooling False Bay winds reach the vines in the afternoon. Its old co-operative cellar is now Stellenbosch Hills, and the ward's Bordeaux varieties and Chenin Blanc benefit from afternoon sea breezes.
za-vlottenburg.terroir: Alluvial and shale-derived soils on gentle slopes.

za-voor-paardeberg.name: Voor-Paardeberg
za-voor-paardeberg.summary: The southern and eastern side ('voor', in front of) the Paardeberg, the granite massif between Paarl and the Swartland. Old dry-land bush vines of Chenin, Cinsault and Shiraz supply many of the Cape's new-wave winemakers.
za-voor-paardeberg.terroir: Decomposed granite over clay, dry farmed; warm and windy.

za-vredendal.name: Vredendal
za-vredendal.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinotage
za-vredendal.summary: The ward around Vredendal in the lower Olifants River, home to Namaqua Wines, one of the largest cellars in South Africa. Namaqua Wines, formed by merging the Vredendal and Spruitdrift co-operatives, is one of the country's largest producers of inexpensive bottled and boxed wine.

za-walker-bay.name: Walker Bay
za-walker-bay.grapes: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinotage, Shiraz
za-walker-bay.summary: The district around the whale-watching town of Hermanus, best known for the Hemel-en-Aarde ('heaven and earth') valley, where Tim Hamilton Russell planted Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in 1975 and made the Cape's first serious Burgundy-style wines. Walker Bay now has seven wards: Hemel-en-Aarde Valley, Upper Hemel-en-Aarde Valley, Hemel-en-Aarde Ridge, Bot River, Stanford Foothills, Springfontein Rim and Sunday's Glen. Its Pinotage is also highly regarded.
za-walker-bay.terroir: Weathered Bokkeveld shale and decomposed granite; strong maritime influence and wind from Walker Bay.

za-wellington.name: Wellington
za-wellington.grapes: Pinotage, Shiraz, Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-wellington.summary: A district north of Paarl at the foot of the Hawequa mountains, about 45 minutes from Cape Town. It supplies more than 85 percent of South Africa's vine cuttings from its nurseries, and its 30 or so producers range from historic estates to Diemersfontein, which created 'coffee Pinotage' in 2001. Its five wards (Blouvlei, Bovlei, Groenberg, Limietberg and Mid-Berg River) were added recently.
za-wellington.terroir: Alluvial terraces along the Berg River and granite and sandstone foothills; snow on the peaks in winter, cooler nights than the coast.

za-western-cape.name: Western Cape
za-western-cape.grapes: Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Colombard, Shiraz, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinotage, Chardonnay
za-western-cape.summary: The Western Cape geographical unit holds almost all of South Africa's wine grapes. 'WO Western Cape' on a label means a blend from two or more of its regions, and many large brands use it.

za-worcester.name: Worcester
za-worcester.summary: The Worcester district is the brandy capital of South Africa, with the largest distillery of its kind in the Southern Hemisphere, and a major source of bulk and branded wine. It has seven wards: Hex River Valley, Keeromsberg, Moordkuil, Nuy, Rooikrans, Scherpenheuvel and Stettyn.

za-zandrivier.name: Zandrivier
za-zandrivier.grapes: Chardonnay, Colombard, Sauvignon Blanc, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon
za-zandrivier.summary: A ward of the Robertson district. Robertson's wards share its lime-rich soils and warm, dry, wind-cooled climate. Most Robertson wards are small, river-centred farming communities whose growers deliver to co-operative cellars such as Robertson Winery, Rooiberg and Van Loveren, and the names rarely appear on labels; the district's reputation rests on Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Cap Classique, fortified Muscadel and increasingly Shiraz and Cabernet.

sites.name: Company's Garden
sites.text: The VOC's vegetable garden, laid out in 1652 to supply passing ships, where Jan van Riebeeck planted the colony's first vines from 1655. On 2 February 1659 he wrote in his diary that wine had been pressed from Cape grapes for the first time. The garden is now a public park in central Cape Town.

sites.name: Castle of Good Hope
sites.text: The VOC's pentagonal stone fort, built between 1666 and 1679, the oldest surviving colonial building in South Africa. Wine for the garrison and the Company's ships was stored and traded from here.

sites.name: Groot Constantia
sites.text: Simon van der Stel was granted Constantia in 1685 and planted the Cape's first great vineyard here. After his death in 1712 the estate was split; Hendrik Cloete bought this part in 1778, built the cellar (1791) with a pediment by Anton Anreith, and made the Constantia wine Napoleon drank on St Helena. The government bought it in 1885; it now makes Grand Constance and red and white table wines.

sites.name: Klein Constantia
sites.text: Part of Van der Stel's original estate. Duggie Jooste bought the run-down farm in 1980, replanted Muscat de Frontignan and released the revived Vin de Constance in 1986, recreating the legendary unfortified sweet wine of the eighteenth century. It also makes fine Sauvignon Blanc from slopes high on the Constantiaberg.

sites.name: Buitenverwachting
sites.text: Another portion of Van der Stel's Constantia, its name means 'beyond expectation'. Revived from 1981 by the Mueller family, it makes Sauvignon Blanc, Christine (a Bordeaux blend) and, since 2007, its own Constantia sweet wine, 1769.

sites.name: Steenberg
sites.text: The oldest farm in the Constantia valley, granted in 1682 to Catharina Ras, a widow who arrived at the Cape in 1662 and outlived several husbands. Today it is a hotel, golf estate and winery known for Sauvignon Blanc and Cap Classique.

sites.name: Cape Point Vineyards
sites.text: Vineyards at Noordhoek on the Cape Peninsula's Atlantic side, some only about 1.2 km from the sea. Planted in the 1990s by Sybrand van der Spuy, they make taut, saline Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon (Isliedh).

sites.name: Diemersdal
sites.text: A Durbanville estate farmed by the Louw family for six generations since 1885, dry-farmed on red granite and shale soils. Thys Louw made it a leader in Sauvignon Blanc, including a Sauvignon from 1992 plantings.

sites.name: Kanonkop
sites.text: On the lower slopes of the Simonsberg, Kanonkop takes its name from a hill where a cannon was fired to tell farmers a VOC ship had arrived. Paul Sauer, a cabinet minister, and Jan 'Boland' Coetzee and Beyers Truter built its reputation; its Pinotage, from bush vines planted in 1953, and Paul Sauer Bordeaux blend are South African classics. It makes red wine only.

sites.name: Rustenberg
sites.text: A farm on the Simonsberg slopes first planted in the 1680s; the Barlow family has owned it since 1941. Its gabled Cape Dutch homestead and old cellars sit below the mountain, and under Simon Barlow it became a leading producer of Cabernet and Chardonnay (Five Soldiers).

sites.name: Thelema
sites.text: Gyles and Barbara Webb bought this fruit farm on the Helshoogte Pass in 1983 and made Thelema one of the first post-isolation stars with Cabernet and Merlot from steep, red granite slopes.

sites.name: Tokara
sites.text: A modern estate at the top of the Helshoogte Pass founded by banker GT Ferreira in the 1990s, with vineyards on the Simonsberg and in Elgin; known for its Director's Reserve blends and olive oil.

sites.name: Warwick
sites.text: Stan and Norma Ratcliffe bought Warwick on the northern Simonsberg in 1964; Norma became one of South Africa's first female winemakers and made the Trilogy Bordeaux blend. The Ratcliffe family sold the estate in 2017.

sites.name: Delheim
sites.text: Hans Otto Hoheisen built this estate on the Simonsberg in the 1940s, and Michael 'Spatz' Sperling, who arrived from Germany in 1951, turned it into one of Stellenbosch's best-loved family estates and helped found the Stellenbosch Wine Route in 1971.

sites.name: Meerlust
sites.text: The Myburgh family has owned Meerlust, south of Stellenbosch near False Bay, since 1756; the farm was granted in 1693. Nico Myburgh and winemaker Giorgio Dalla Cia created Rubicon, a Bordeaux blend first made in 1980, which became one of South Africa's defining reds.

sites.name: Vergelegen
sites.text: Governor Willem Adriaan van der Stel, Simon's son, built Vergelegen in 1700 on the slopes of the Hottentots Holland mountains; his abuse of office led to his recall in 1707. Anglo American bought the estate in 1987, and its hilltop winery (opened 1992) makes Vergelegen V and GVB, among the Cape's finest Bordeaux blends. Camphor trees planted around 1700 still stand.

sites.name: Rust en Vrede
sites.text: A small red-wine estate on the Helderberg foothills, owned by the Engelbrecht family since 1977 (rugby player Jannie Engelbrecht). Its 1694 farm buildings and Estate blend of Cabernet, Shiraz and Merlot are Stellenbosch classics.

sites.name: Spier
sites.text: One of the oldest farms in Stellenbosch, first granted in 1692, with a 1767 wine cellar among South Africa's oldest. Today it is a large winery, hotel and arts centre with a focus on sustainability and community development.

sites.name: Lanzerac
sites.text: A gabled Cape Dutch estate at the mouth of the Jonkershoek Valley, dating from 1692. Its name became famous in 1961, when Stellenbosch Farmers' Winery released a Pinotage made from Bellevue grapes under the Lanzerac label, the first wine ever to name Pinotage on its label.

sites.name: Kleine Zalze
sites.text: A Stellenbosch estate farmed since 1695 and revived by the Basson family from 1996. Its Family Reserve Chenin Blanc and Sauvignon Blanc are regular award winners, and its cellar door sits on the De Zalze golf estate.

sites.name: Ken Forrester
sites.text: Ken Forrester, a restaurateur from Johannesburg, bought the 1689 farm Scholtzenhof on the Helderberg in 1993 and became 'Mr Chenin', championing old-vine Chenin Blanc. His FMC (with the Meinert family) showed that barrel-fermented, botrytis-touched Chenin could rank with the world's great whites.

sites.name: Welgevallen Experimental Farm
sites.text: Stellenbosch University's experimental farm, where Professor Abraham Perold crossed Pinot Noir with Cinsaut (then called Hermitage) in 1925 to create Pinotage. The seedlings were nearly lost when Perold left for the KWV in 1927; a colleague, Charlie Niehaus, rescued them from the overgrown garden.

sites.name: Simonsig
sites.text: The Malan family's estate north of Stellenbosch, where Frans Malan made Kaapse Vonkel from the 1971 vintage, South Africa's first bottle-fermented sparkling wine, beginning the Méthode Cap Classique category.

sites.name: Boschendal
sites.text: Granted in 1685 to the Huguenot Jean le Long and owned for a century by the de Villiers family, Boschendal is one of the Cape's most visited estates. Its 1812 manor house is a showpiece of Cape Dutch architecture, and its farm now combines wine with orchards, livestock and food.

sites.name: Huguenot Monument
sites.text: A monument at the head of Franschhoek, completed in 1948, commemorating the French Protestant refugees who settled here from 1688. The adjacent museum records the families, many of whose descendants still farm Cape vineyards.

sites.name: Boekenhoutskloof
sites.text: A Franschhoek farm founded in 1776 whose name refers to the native Cape beech (boekenhout). Marc Kent built it into one of South Africa's leading producers from the 1990s, with Syrah, Cabernet, Sémillon from vines planted in 1902 and 1942, and the value brands The Chocolate Block and Porcupine Ridge. It also owns Porseleinberg in the Swartland.

sites.name: KWV Cathedral Cellar
sites.text: The KWV, founded in 1918, built its headquarters in Paarl; the Cathedral Cellar (1930) has a vaulted roof and carved vats depicting the history of Cape wine. Its 'emporium' complex also houses some of the largest wine vats in the world.

sites.name: Nederburg
sites.text: Founded in 1791 near Paarl, Nederburg was modernised by German winemaker Günter Brözel from 1956 and hosted the Nederburg Auction, South Africa's main fine-wine auction, from 1975.

sites.name: Fairview
sites.text: Charles Back's family estate on the slopes of Paarl Mountain, famous for its goats (and Goats do Roam wine), cheese and Rhône varieties. Back also founded Spice Route in the Swartland in 1998, an early bet on the district.

sites.name: Sadie Family Wines
sites.text: Eben Sadie's farm and cellar on the Paardeberg, where he makes Columella (Syrah-led, first vintage 2000), Palladius (a white blend from 2002) and the Old Vineyard Series of single-site wines from old vines across the Cape. Sadie became the face of the Swartland's revival.

sites.name: A.A. Badenhorst, Kalmoesfontein
sites.text: Adi Badenhorst and his cousin Hein bought the run-down Kalmoesfontein farm on the Paardeberg in 2008, restoring a 1930s cellar and old bush vines of Chenin, Cinsault and Grenache. The Secateurs range and the Family white and red blends made them stars of the Swartland Revolution.

sites.name: Mullineux, Roundstone
sites.text: Chris and Andrea Mullineux arrived in the Swartland in 2007 and farm the Roundstone vineyard near Riebeek-Kasteel on schist and iron-rich soils. Their Syrah and old-vine Chenin, and single-terroir bottlings showing granite, schist and iron, are benchmarks; Andrea was named Wine Enthusiast's winemaker of the year in 2016.

sites.name: Porseleinberg
sites.text: A farm on the blue-grey schist of the 'porcelain mountain' bought by Boekenhoutskloof in 2009, where Callie Louw farms Syrah organically and ferments it in concrete eggs and foudres. Its Porseleinberg Syrah (first vintage 2010) is one of South Africa's most sought-after reds; the label is printed on a hand-operated press on the farm.

sites.name: Riebeek-Kasteel
sites.text: A Swartland village below the Kasteelberg where the Swartland Revolution festival was held from 2010 to 2015, bringing wine writers and sommeliers from around the world to taste old-vine Chenin, Cinsault and Syrah.

sites.name: Hamilton Russell Vineyards
sites.text: Tim Hamilton Russell, an advertising executive, bought land in the Hemel-en-Aarde Valley in 1975 to make Burgundy-style wine, at a time when Pinot Noir and Chardonnay imports were restricted. His son Anthony and wife Olive built the estate's reputation; its Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, from stony, clay-rich shale, are South African benchmarks.

sites.name: Bouchard Finlayson
sites.text: Peter Finlayson, who made Hamilton Russell's first wines, founded this estate in 1989 with Burgundian Paul Bouchard. Its Galpin Peak Pinot Noir and Hannibal blend are well known, and its Kaaimansgat Chardonnay comes from high vineyards near Villiersdorp.

sites.name: Newton Johnson
sites.text: The Newton Johnson family's estate in the Upper Hemel-en-Aarde Valley, founded in 1996, makes some of South Africa's most admired Pinot Noir (Family Vineyards) from granite and shale slopes.

sites.name: Creation
sites.text: Swiss winemaker Jean-Claude Martin and his wife Carolyn planted Creation on the Hemel-en-Aarde Ridge in 2002 on virgin land, and it has become one of the area's leading Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producers.

sites.name: Alheit Vineyards, Hemelrand
sites.text: Chris and Suzaan Alheit make their wines on the Hemelrand farm at the top of the Hemel-en-Aarde, but source old vines across the Cape. Their Cartology blend of old-vine Chenin and Sémillon (from 2011) and single-vineyard Chenins such as Magnetic North, from the high Skurfberg in Citrusdal Mountain, are among the most acclaimed whites in South Africa.

sites.name: Magnetic North (Skurfberg)
sites.text: A dry-farmed bush-vine Chenin Blanc vineyard on the sandstone of the Skurfberg, high above Clanwilliam in the Citrusdal Mountain district. Chris Alheit's Magnetic North and Eben Sadie's Skurfberg both come from this cold, windy, sandy plateau.

sites.name: Paul Cluver
sites.text: Dr Paul Cluver, a neurosurgeon, planted vines on his family's apple farm in Elgin in 1987 and made Elgin's first wines; the estate is known for Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and botrytised Riesling, and for its amphitheatre concerts.

sites.name: Elim Moravian Mission
sites.text: A mission village founded by Moravian missionaries in 1824 near Cape Agulhas. Its thatched cottages and church are a national monument, and the windswept Elim ward around it gives some of the Cape's coolest Sauvignon Blanc.

sites.name: Boplaas
sites.text: The Nel family has farmed at Calitzdorp since 1880. Carel Nel built Boplaas's fame for Cape Vintage and Cape Tawny made from Touriga Nacional and Tinta Barocca, and the family also distills potstill brandy and whisky.

sites.name: De Krans
sites.text: Another Nel family farm in Calitzdorp, known for Cape Vintage Reserve, Cape Tawny and dry Portuguese-variety table wines. Calitzdorp hosts an annual 'Port and Wine Festival'.

sites.name: Graham Beck, Madeba
sites.text: Mining magnate Graham Beck bought the Madeba farm near Robertson in 1983; under Pieter Ferreira ('Bubbles') it became South Africa's leading Cap Classique house, whose sparkling wine was served at Nelson Mandela's inauguration in 1994.

sites.name: Cederberg Private Cellar
sites.text: The Nieuwoudt family's farm at Dwarsrivier in the Cederberg mountains, with vineyards at about 1,000 m among some of the highest in South Africa. Planted from the 1970s, they make crisp Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin and Shiraz.

sites.name: Groote Post
sites.text: A historic dairy farm in the Darling hills that Peter Pentz and his son Nick turned to vines in the 1990s, a few kilometres from the Atlantic. Cool Atlantic air gives its Sauvignon Blanc a reputation for freshness.

sites.name: Saronsberg
sites.text: A Tulbagh estate at the foot of the Saronsberg on the valley's northern edge, bought by Nick van Huyssteen in 2002 and replanted with Rhône varieties. Its Shiraz and Full Circle blend show the valley's warm days and cold-trap nights.
